author: Qari Syed Hussain
title: A friend's tribute to Dr. Ahmad Tabassum
titleOriginal: حاجی الحرمین الشریف ڈاکٹر محمد احمد تبسم صاحب
takeaway: A man remembered for serving people, helping the poor and feeling others' pain.
scene: This poem is not by Dr. Ahmad. It was written in Urdu by his close friend Qari Syed Hussain, as a tribute to him. The heading calls him 'Haji al-Haramain', meaning he had made the pilgrimage to both holy mosques, in Makkah and Madinah. The note under the title says: 'He is my dear old friend and benefactor. Because of his kindness to me, I express my heartfelt feelings.'

original: محمد احمد کتنا پیارا نام ہے
ہر وقت گردش میں ان کا جام ہے
transliteration: Muhammad Ahmad kitna pyaara naam hai
Har waqt gardish mein un ka jaam hai
translation: Muhammad Ahmad: what a lovely name!
His cup is always being passed around.
couplets.story: His friend starts with his name, Muhammad Ahmad, and says what a lovely name it is. His 'cup' is always going round, meaning his generosity is always being shared with others.

original: خدمت خلق اسکا فیض عام ہے
یہ ہمیشہ کام صبح و شام ہے
translation: Serving people is his blessing to all;
it's his work, always, morning and evening.
couplets.story: Helping people is his gift to everyone. He does it all day, every day.

original: ڈاکٹر احمد بڑے ہیں خوش نصیب
حاجی الحرمین بھی ہیں اور ادیب
translation: he has made the pilgrimage to both holy mosques, and he is a man of letters.
couplets.story: Dr. Ahmad is blessed. He has been on pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah, and he's also a writer.

original: لڑکا ان کا ایک ہے خلف رشید
وہ بھی مثل بدر ہے بے حد سعید
transliteration: Larka un ka ek hai khalaf-e-rasheed
Woh bhi misl-e-badr hai be-had saeed
translation: He has one son, a fine and worthy heir;
he too is like the full moon, and greatly blessed.
couplets.story: He has one son, who is a good and worthy young man, as bright as the full moon and very blessed.

original: غریبوں کی امداد ان کا کام ہے
اسلیئے دنیا میں ان کا نام ہے
transliteration: Gareebon ki imdaad un ka kaam hai
Is liye duniya mein un ka naam hai
translation: Helping the poor is his work;
that's why his name is known in the world.
couplets.story: Helping poor people is what he does, and that's why everyone knows his name.

original: درد دل دنیا میں رکھتے ہیں کمال
transliteration: Dard-e-dil duniya mein rakhte hain kamaal
translation: He has a remarkable heart that feels others' pain;
good in character, cheerful by nature, content.
couplets.story: He truly feels other people's pain. He's a good person, cheerful and content.

original: ایسے لوگوں کی نہیں ملتی مثال
جو غریبوں کا رکھیں ہر دم خیال
transliteration: Aise logon ki nahin milti misaal
Jo gareebon ka rakhen har dam khayaal
translation: There's no finding another example of people like this,
who look after the poor at every moment.
couplets.story: You won't find many people like him, who always look out for the poor.

original: ہے دعا قاری کی اے میرے خدا
درد کی لذت سے کر دے آشنا
transliteration: Hai duaa Qaari ki, ae mere Khuda
Dard ki lazzat se kar de aashna
translation: This is the Qari's prayer: O my God,
let me know the sweetness of feeling others' pain.
couplets.story: His friend, the Qari, ends with a prayer. Dear God, let me feel the same 'sweetness' Dr. Ahmad felt in caring about other people's pain.

deeper: The final prayer, to know 'the sweetness of pain' (lazzat-e-dard), sums up how Dr. Ahmad's friends saw him: a man who found meaning in carrying other people's pain. It's the same idea that runs through his own poems, where caring for others is the truest form of love for God.
why: It's one of the best portraits of the poet in the book: a doctor who served the poor and felt their pain.
prompt: What would you want a friend to write about you one day?
notes: Written by Qari Syed Hussain, described at the bottom as 'Dr. Ahmad Tabassum's admirer'.
Printed in two columns; each row is one couplet.
